_comment: People whose cost is NOT in the Victorian payroll tax base.
WHY THIS FILE CHANGED SHAPE (3 September 2026). It used to be a bare list
of names, compared to the invoice or bill line DESCRIPTION, exactly. On a
payroll row Description is the employee's name, so it worked there and
looked fine. On a sales or bill line Description is whatever the line says
- 'Rajeev Jindal - Solution Architect', a PO number, a date range - and an
exact string comparison misses every one of them. Those lines fell through
to Payable: $95,876.29 wrongly in the base in July FY27 alone.
The matching now happens on the ITEM CODE, which is the one stable key.
The names below are resolved to their Xero item codes once, at load, by
exact name match - see mappers.exempt_item_codes. Name matching here is
STRICT: a near miss would grant somebody else's exemption and take money
out of the base, so a name that does not match an item exactly is REPORTED
rather than guessed at. Run tracking_diagnostics() to see which names found
no item code.
names      - keep maintaining this. It is how the exemption is thought
about, and every name that resolves to an item is matched on
the code from then on. A name that resolves to nothing still
falls back to the old description match, so nothing regressed
- but it is a silent miss waiting to happen, and
tracking_diagnostics names it.
item_codes - the explicit answer for anyone the name path cannot reach: no
inventory item at all, or a Xero item Name that does not read
like the person's name. A code here needs no name. The leading
z of a retired item is folded away, so 'Linfox - DC' also
covers 'zLinfox - DC'.
A bare JSON list still loads, so an older copy of this file cannot quietly
empty the exemption list.
This is a lodgement figure. Check it against a lodged return before
relying on it.
